overall: Atlanta is running significantly cooler than expected this morning, sitting at just 73.4°F at 10:00 ET under complete overcast skies with an exceptionally low ceiling of 122m (~400 feet), suggesting dense stratus or fog rather than typical morning cloud cover. Despite this suppression, the 30-minute velocity has spiked to +3.6°F/hr, hinting the low cloud deck may be beginning to erode. The running max has been locked at 73.4°F since at least 7:00 ET, meaning no meaningful daytime heating has occurred yet.
forecast_obs_notes: The NWS official forecast of 88°F and 'mostly sunny' skies is in notable tension with the current OVC/100% cloud-fraction reality; NWP models are already cooler — HRRR at 83.4°F, ECMWF at 85.5°F, NBM at 86.4°F — and even these may be optimistic if the low stratus deck lingers past midday. The META probability distribution peaks at 84–85°F (25.1%) with substantial mass in the 86–89°F range, reflecting the genuine uncertainty between a full cloud-burn scenario and a partial one.
max_temp_prediction: The key driver today is how quickly and completely the overcast deck lifts: if clouds clear by noon, temps can surge toward 86–88°F given the strong latent heating and a predicted peak hour near 14:00–15:00 ET; if stratus persists through early afternoon, the high is more likely in the 82–84°F range. Weighting the NWP model consensus (~85°F average), the META bucket peak at 84–85°F, and the encouraging +3.6°F/hr short-term velocity, a best estimate lands near 85°F with below-average confidence given the cloud-cover wildcard.
